newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business leaders express concern on dollar.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business leaders express concern on dollar.

text.p: Members of the U.S. Business Council on Thursday signaled some concern about the potential for a further rise in the dollar against the yen.

Asked about the currency at a Business Council news conference, Larry Bossidy, chairman and chief executive of AlliedSignal Inc, said he would be comfortable with the dollar at 110 yen but would not like to see it go much higher.

"I'd like it (the dollar) at parity (100) but 110 is not going to change the landscape dramatically," Bossidy said. "If it continues to widen and is followed by an increase (against) other currencies, for example the deutschmark, that would have a significant impact on our competitiveness."
Given that the dollar is now slightly above 112 yen, Bossidy and other members said they were a bit uneasy about the potential trendline.
Du Pont Chairman Edgar Woolard, who also chairs the Business Council, added, "If 112 is on the way to 120, it's a concern."
The Business Council represents leaders from 100 of the largest U.S. corporations.
